messages:
maria - Support: customer on Private (VPC) reporting intermittent TLS handshake failures to our embeddings endpoint from behind their corp LB. curl fails with SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL.

alex - Eng Runtime: can you paste the curl + verbose output and an openssl s_client from their environment? usually need ClientHello to debug.

maria - Support: here's the minimal repro they ran:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \\n  --data '{"input":"hi"}'
* SSL connect error
* Closing connection 0
```
They also ran: 
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -tls1_2
CONNECTED(00000003)
139736... handshake failure
```

tao - Eng Security: sounds like a cipher mismatch. Do they terminate TLS at the LB and re-encrypt upstream? If the LB enforces server-preferred cipher order and strips TLS1.3 ciphers, old clients can fail. Ask for their LB TLS profile.

ingrid - Eng SRE: also need the ClientHello supported_groups and signature_algorithms. If their client advertises only RSA+legacy ciphers and our server prefers ECDSA/TLS1.3-only suites, no overlap. Can you get a packet capture of ClientHello? tcpdump filter: `tcp port 443 and host <client_ip>` and upload pcap.

maria - Support: customer says they run a managed F5 that applies a strict profile (RSA-first, disables some ECDHE curves). Their app is Java8u131 with a custom https stack. They pasted this log from the LB: `SSL Handshake failed: no shared cipher`.

sam - DevEx: common quick workaround: force the client JVM to enable additional ciphers and curves: `-Dhttps.protocols=TLSv1.2 -Djdk.tls.client.protocols=TLSv1.2 -Djdk.tls.client.enableCAExtension=true` and optionally set `-Djdk.tls.client.cipherSuites=TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` (depends on vendor). For curl: `--tlsv1.2 --ciphers 'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256'`.

alex - Eng Runtime: we can also temporarily enable an alternate endpoint that accepts older ciphers for this enterprise customer (short-term) but we need approval from security. Tao, any objections?

tao - Eng Security: accepting legacy ciphers on our public endpoint is a risk. Prefer customers to update their LB or allowlist our egress so their proxy can passthrough TLS. If they're in Private mode, they can add a bypass route in their VPC egress ACLs to our dedicated edge IPs.

maria - Support: repro steps I asked them to run and share:
1) `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -tls1_2 -cipher 'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256' -msg` and paste ClientHello
2) `tcpdump -w /tmp/handshake.pcap tcp port 443 and host <client>`
3) sample java run: `java -Dhttps.protocols=TLSv1.2 -Djdk.tls.client.cipherSuites=TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 -jar app.jar`

ingrid - Eng SRE: escalate to their infra team to loosen the LB TLS profile or enable ECDHE curves (secp256r1/secp384r1) and TLS1.2 AEAD ciphers. If they can't, customer can add a VPC-level NAT rule to bypass the proxy for our egress IPs.

maria - Support: opened support case CASE-12345 and asked for pcap + s_client. customer replied they will test enabling ECDHE suites.

oncall-bot: reminder: escalate to enterprise success and add to case.

(4 hours later)

maria - Support: update — customer changed F5 TLS profile to allow ECDHE-RSA and enabled secp256r1. they re-ran openssl s_client and got `Verify return code: 0 (ok)`. traffic now passes. :tada:

alex - Eng Runtime: thanks! please include the LB config they changed in the case notes so we can add a KB entry for Private customers behind managed LBs.

maria - Support: will add details and a suggested KB template: why client Hello vs server order matters, repro commands, and recommended LB profile (TLS1.2 AEAD + ECDHE + curves).

sam - DevEx: adding note to quickstart Private network guide: include JVM flags and curl snippets for TLS troubleshooting.

ingrid - Eng SRE: closing loop — mark case RESOLVED after customer confirmation.
